features.title: Integration mode
features.description:
The integration consists of two parts that work independently — you can use both or just one. A failure in one part never stops the other.

**MT_SW panel** — an app in the Home Assistant sidebar that works like the Meshtastic app on your phone: channel and direct messages, a list of all nodes with favourites, map, neighbours, radio settings, sniffer and OnDemand diagnostics. It creates no entities.

**Statistics** — Home Assistant devices and entities for the selected nodes: battery, voltage, signal (SNR/RSSI), channel utilisation, environment telemetry, position on the HA map and notify entities for sending messages. History, graphs, dashboard cards and automations are built on them.

You can change the mode at any time later: **Settings → Devices & services → MT_SW_INTEGRATION → Configure**.

data_description.mode: Most people pick the first option. With “Panel only” you skip choosing nodes and notify entities.

data_description.mode: After disabling statistics, existing devices and entities stay in Home Assistant as unavailable — you can remove them manually. After disabling the panel it disappears from the sidebar; message history is kept on disk.
data_description.nodes: Nodes for which Home Assistant creates devices and entities (sensors, tracker, notifications). Click the field to add a node from the radio's node database; the cross next to a node stops tracking it. Only matters in a mode with statistics — the panel always shows all nodes.

web_client.name: MT_SW web client
web_client.description: The MT_SW web client (built on the official Meshtastic web client) served through Home Assistant — it connects to the integration instead of the radio directly (the radio accepts only one connection). WARNING: the Meshtastic protocol has no authentication — anyone with access to your Home Assistant can then control the gateway.

data_description.enable: Once enabled, open the client from the Radio tab of the MT_SW panel.
data_description.port: Port the web client uses to reach the integration. Default 4408.

tcp_proxy.name: TCP proxy
tcp_proxy.description: Shares the radio with other programs (app, Meshtastic CLI) through Home Assistant without dropping the integration's connection — the radio accepts only one connection. WARNING: the Meshtastic protocol has no authentication — anyone on your network who can reach this port can control the gateway.

data_description.enable: Programs then connect to Home Assistant's address, e.g. meshtastic --host homeassistant:4403.
data_description.port: Port on which Home Assistant accepts connections. Default 4403.
